entries.title: Het Veilinghuisje, the house everyone thought was demolished
entries.hook: A booksellers' auction house hidden in an inner court, believed demolished in 1989 and still standing.

entries.title: Blaauwlakenblok, the block the squatters held and the residents rebuilt
entries.hook: The Bijenkorf wanted it for offices; squatters held it; sixty houses restored with W139 and the Condomerie.

entries.title: The hole in the quay: a 600-year-old sluice under the Nieuwmarkt
entries.hook: A culvert runs under the Waag to a sluice paid for by a polder board 40 km away; fish hall and Bredero beside.

entries.title: The tallest tree in Amsterdam, Oudemanhuispoort courtyard
entries.reason: courtyard open weekdays only; or a Look for in the Oudemanhuispoort draft
entries.hook: A Dutch elm of 1890, 36 m tall and the thickest elm in the city, that thousands of students walk past.

entries.title: The red window of the Oude Kerk ("Het Rode Raam")
entries.reason: beside A-list Oude Kerk, pitched on the fight
entries.hook: One church window turned permanently red, lighting the nave from the Red Light District; heritage societies sued.

entries.title: Pijlsteeg, an alley through a hotel
entries.hook: One of the two streets where prostitution was allowed in 1413, now built over by Krasnapolsky but public.

entries.title: "GOD ROEPT U / JESUS LOVES YOU", the neon over the station square
entries.reason: the astronaut claim rests on the neighbourhood paper
entries.hook: The first words many arrivals read: blue neon on the old Hotel Karsten, said to be switched on by an astronaut.

entries.title: Belle and the bronze breast, Oudekerksplein
entries.reason: 1993 date and anonymity rest on blogs
entries.hook: The first statue of a sex worker, a groping bronze hand set into the paving, and the PIC next door.

entries.title: Trompettersteeg, the narrowest alley and its hidden coat of arms
entries.hook: Dopie's anamorphic city arms come right from one spot only; blacked out in anger, restored in 2021.

entries.title: Majoor Bosshardt on her bench
entries.hook: The Salvation Army officer of the Wallen sits on a bench drunk tourists would not leave alone.

entries.title: Chet Baker's window, Hotel Prins Hendrik
entries.hook: The trumpeter fell from a window here in 1988; fans put up an illegal trumpet pole, then a plaque.

entries.title: Koestraat, "Ons Dorp", the street with its own mayor
entries.hook: Residents crown a street mayor in Sweelinck's old garden; a 1912 stone for the inventor of the fire hose.

entries.title: He Hua temple and the Chinese Zeedijk
entries.hook: A Chinese Buddhist temple on the dike, "a striking stranger on the Zeedijk", with the Vesak procession.

entries.title: Bet van Beeren, 't Mandje and Hartjesdag on the Zeedijk
entries.hook: The café of Bet van Beeren, a bridge named after her, and the Zeedijk's revived drag street party.

entries.title: Mata Hari and the Determeyer skybridge
entries.hook: A uniform maker's 1929 bridge over the Korte Niezel, later the roof of an illegal gambling palace.

entries.title: Apotheek Van der Meulen, a pharmacy since 1696
entries.hook: Apothecaries on this corner without a break since 1696, the 1880 interior in its original blue.

entries.title: Spooksteeg, the ghost of the Zeedijk
entries.hook: Wailing nobody could trace drew crowds in 1853, and the alley was renamed Ghost Alley.

entries.title: Oudezijds Voorburgwal 61, four hundred years without piles
entries.hook: Stadsherstel found no piles at all: the walls stand straight on the ground.

entries.title: Geldersekade 78, the swindler Barmat
entries.hook: Home of the swindler Hitler used as a bogeyman in his propaganda.

entries.title: The murder of Magere Josje, 1957
entries.reason: Okay; single source; handle with care
entries.hook: A sex worker's murder in 1957 that young detective Baantjer never solved.

entries.title: Oudezijds Armsteeg "street gallery"
entries.reason: may be gone; pin not set
entries.hook: Residents turned a dumping corner into an open-air gallery of small vitrines in 2013.

entries.title: "Wandelend naar de Nieuwmarkt", the brick walkers on the Varkenssluis
entries.hook: Brick walkers of 1986, vandalised and remade in 2011 as four Chinese walkers with a lion dance.

entries.title: Bureau Warmoesstraat, the police station of Baantjer
entries.hook: Baantjer's police station, closed after a man put out on the pavement died; a plaque on the sandwich shop since 2025.

entries.title: Stoofbrug and the 3D-printed bridge
entries.hook: MX3D's printed steel bridge lay here two years; the lost old bridge was found and came back in 2024.

entries.title: Heintje Hoekssteeg, the alley that got its gate
entries.reason: Okay; beside A-list Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder
entries.hook: An alley used as a public toilet, now closed with a gate (2026).

entries.title: Jacob Hooy & Co., the drugstore of 1743
entries.hook: A herb and sweet shop with drawers and barrels unchanged since the 18th century.

enrich.draft: Beursplein 5, the stock exchange that left Berlage
enrich.add: the Walraven van Hall plaque (1949) and Stauthamer's "Ex tenebris lux" inside; the clock the Germans shot (access to check)

enrich.draft: Sint-Olofskapel, the sailors' chapel that became a hotel's meeting hall
enrich.add: the houses on the gate site: Sint Olofspoort 1 (c. 1605) uses the chapel's west wall as its back wall; nos. 9-15 sold 1618

enrich.draft: Barndesteeg, the penitents' convent and the mission hostel
enrich.add: the 1450 crypt, the nuns' cows that named the Koestraat, the first Hare Krishna temple (1970)

enrich.draft: Spinhuis, the women's prison and its whipping gate
enrich.add: Look for: the wall of the vanished church De Star in the Spinhuissteeg
the alley Gebed zonder End: convent name, sign painted on the wall because it kept being stolen

enrich.draft: Walloon Church and its gate of skulls
enrich.add: the Walenpleintje: hidden court behind the gate, named only in 1978, open by day
the VOC room dismantled without a permit and the VVAB enforcement request (VVAB news 707, 2026)
the UvA war memorial in the garden (254 students, 28 staff; year to confirm); the cholera house of the 1830s

enrich.draft: Huis aan de Drie Grachten and its wartime bookshop
enrich.add: Look for: the oldest lampposts on the Grimburgwal quay, fished out after the 2020 collapse (back yet?)

enrich.draft: Kleinste huis (the smallest house), Oude Hoogstraat 22
enrich.add: also Klein Trippenhuis (the little Trip house)
